title: Service SLA variance by route and seqlen
body:
Purpose and context:

This is a working note summarizing recent trace-based sampling across product routes to understand why observed Service-level latency (p50/p95/p99) diverges by route and sequence-length distribution. Goal: identify the dominant stage-level contributors for the slow tails and produce a short experiment plan to reduce p95/p99 by 20% for the top two failing cohorts.

Summary findings (top-level):
- Aggregate (all routes, last 7d sample): p50=130ms, p95=480ms, p99=1.9s.
- Chat route (conversational streaming): p50=95ms, p95=420ms, p99=1.6s. Tail dominated by batching_wait + model_forward for medium-long sequences.
- Completions (single-shot): p50=200ms, p95=730ms, p99=2.5s. We see a bimodal distribution tied to seq_len<=64 vs seq_len>256.
- Embeddings: p50=70ms, p95=150ms, p99=420ms. Variance driven by input preproc (tokenization) when documents are long, and by microburst queueing on the small-GPU pool.

Per-stage decomposition (representative cohort: completions, seq_len 256-1024, model variant quantized-8bit):
- request-parse: p50=3ms, p95=8ms, p99=20ms
- tokenization: p50=6ms, p95=18ms, p99=70ms
- routing/authorization: p50=4ms, p95=12ms, p99=30ms
- batching_wait: p50=20ms, p95=220ms, p99=800ms  <-- dominant tail contributor for this cohort
- kv-cache-lookup: p50=2ms, p95=10ms, p99=45ms
- model_forward (incl attention & kv writes): p50=120ms, p95=260ms, p99=760ms
- postprocess/response-encode: p50=10ms, p95=25ms, p99=90ms
- egress/network: p50=5ms, p95=30ms, p99=70ms

Notes on interpretation:
- batching_wait here is the time a request spends waiting to enter a GPU batch. It has heavy variance when traffic is spiky or when autoscaling delays create intermittent capacity crunches. In the p99 case we observed batching_wait+model_forward adding up to >1.5s.
- model_forward variance increases with sequence length (quadratic-ish for attention cost), but batching_wait amplifies its impact on tail because longer sequences come out of larger batches and sometimes hit preemption/queueing artifacts.

Cohort breakdowns and surprising contrasts:
- Short requests (seq_len <= 64): p95 is dominated by scheduling overhead (routing + cold-kv misses) rather than model_forward. p95~210ms, p99~600ms.
- Medium requests (65-256): p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.7s. Both batching_wait and model_forward matter.
- Long requests (>256): median shifts higher; cold-start GPU knee visible when model variant warmup occurs. p95 often >900ms.
- Route-level: chat route shows lower median due to streaming early-token response, but tails are comparable because streaming still waits on first-token batch mechanics for some flows.

Representative trace anecdotes (from sampled traces):
- Trace A (completions, p99): batching_wait=780ms, model_forward=560ms, tokenization=35ms, misc=45ms => total 1.42s; device load at time showed 89% utilization and a single-node outlier with slower kernel startup (suspect NUMA/thread distribution).
- Trace B (chat, p95): batching_wait=320ms (caused by small burst arriving during autoscaler cooldown), model_forward=145ms => total 520ms.

Immediate hypotheses to test:
1) Autoscaler cooldowns are creating transient under-provisioning that increases batching_wait for medium bursts. Test: shorten cooldown and observe p95 delta on small GPU pool.
2) Batch formation algorithm favors throughput over latency for chat route when sequencelens are skewed. Test: enforce seqlen-aware evicting policy to cap batch latency for short sequences.
3) KV cache miss handling adds tail variance due to remote KVS backoff. Test: local LRU warming for hot prefixes and measure p99 changes.
4) Kernel startup overhead on certain hardware/driver combos increases model_forward p99. Test: targeted hotfix kernel prewarm per node and compare p99.

Experiment plan (short-term, 2-week cadence):
- Week 0: create controlled load generator to replay sampled trace cohorts (tools/trace-replay). Reproduce p50/p95/p99 locally and on staging. (Owners: Priya + Diego)
- Week 1: Autoscaler cooldown change: reduce cooldown from 90s -> 30s for small-GPU pool and run 24h A/B on canary traffic. Collect p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization. (Owner: Liam)
- Week 1: Implement seqlen-aware batch cap (soft cap at 128 tokens) for chat path; experiment behind runtime flag for 48h. (Owner: Maya)
- Week 2: Deploy per-node kernel prewarm script on 10% of nodes and run targeted workload; compare model_forward p99. (Owner: Diego)

Observability and instrumentation changes recommended:
- Add new trace tag: cohort.seqlen_bucket = short|medium|long attached at request creation to simplify sampling and filtering.
- Sample 1% of requests always with full trace (already happening) and increase to 5% for routes with p99 > 1s. Use ring buffer to keep top-1000 slow traces/day per route.
- Dashboard additions: per-route waterfall with stacked quantiles per stage (p50/p75/p95/p99) for last 1h/6h/7d.
- Alerting: Add an SLO alert when p95 crosses 25% above baseline for >15m AND total outstanding queue depth > configured threshold.

Risks, open questions and data gaps:
- We still lack per-node kernel timing breakdowns (kernel-init vs execution) in our traces. Need microbenchmarks and flamegraphs on suspect nodes.
- Some traces show correlated network dips in same AZ that align with KV backoff. Is there a transient network fabric issue? Need infra team correlation.
- Does quantization increase variance for medium-long sequences due to kernel selection differences? We need detailed per-variant traces.

Decision checklist (what would make us call this resolved):
- Two independent experiments reduce p95 by >=20% for top failing cohort OR reduce p99 by >=15% without increasing cost >5%.
- New dashboards and trace sampling available for owners and SRE to monitor.
- One follow-up doc produced with concrete rollout plan and rollback criteria.

Notes / links to artifacts for follow-up:
- Trace replay harness: github:repo/serving-runtime/trace-replay (see README and sample-configs)
- Autoscaler PR: github:repo/autoscaler/pull/67 (work-in-progress)
- Kernel prewarm helper: infra:scripts/kernel-prewarm.sh (prototype in PR#411)
- Related Jira: ENG-1429 (latency spikes during autoscaler cooldown)

Action items (owners and tentative due dates):
- Priya: set up cohort-based trace replay and reproducible runbook (due 2026-03-17)
- Liam: deploy autoscaler cooldown canary and collect p95/p99 (due 2026-03-20)
- Diego: implement kernel prewarm on canary nodes and collect detailed kernel timing (due 2026-03-22)
- Maya: implement seqlen-aware batching cap behind feature flag and coordinate A/B (due 2026-03-21)

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- When replaying traces, ensure exact inter-arrival distributions; naive Poisson will not recreate microburst queueing.
- For batch experiments, track batch-size histogram and per-batch composition by seqlen to validate policy effects.

Open questions to ask infra and SRE:
- Can infra provide per-host kernel-init timings for the last 48h? (ask: @infra-kernel)
- Are there any known network maintenance windows that align with observed tail days? (ask: @sre-network)

Status: draft — needs trace replays and two short canary experiments to validate hypotheses.

If you pull a trace and want to discuss, ping me with the trace id and cohort tag.

-- Maya
